author: RATED124563825
title: Good game, but lacking in some areas
content:
Starting with the good:
- Well polished arrow game. Lots of levels, different types of arrows for challenges, and the 3D aspect makes it more interesting to follow arrow paths than a simple 2d board.
- Boards don’t feel unfair. Maybe I’m not far enough in yet at level 132, but no board has felt like a random move I made 100 moves ago screwed me.
- You get boosts regularly through events for free, so even if you got stuck in an unwinnable position, you don’t have to restart or spend money to continue.

Now what it lacks:
- Add a confirm move option in settings. Almost all of my lost hearts are because I was rotating the board and clicked an arrow by mistake. Just have an option where you have to double tap arrows, first tap selects and second tap sends.
- Boards get really repetitive. I know you can do interesting things because some boards are really cool and challenging, like the one level where you had the 4 rotations in a cube, so you had to send arrows in the right order to keep the rotations aligned. Or levels with very weird shapes that make it harder to follow the arrows to the next move. Those are fun.
- Ads are ridiculous. You need ads to make money, that’s fair. But unlike other games, your unrewarded ads take forever to go through. Sometimes it takes me over 30 seconds to get to the final x for an ad that I get nothing from, which was longer than it took me to beat the last level. And the rewarded ads can take 1-2 minutes+. Either make the ads less frequent or faster to skip.
- Lastly, add a board creator. Players can make such cool custom boards. This is the biggest ask, but it would create an actual lively community.

Also a few tips for anyone looking to play:
- Arrows will feel frustrating at first because it’s hard to tell if it will past. Rotate the face to be  perfectly vertical with your screen by circling your finger on the screen. This makes it easier to see the path.
- If two straight arrow heads are pointed directly at each other, they won’t hit each other. 
- When you can’t see the tail of an arrow, check to make sure it’s not a two+ headed arrow. At the start of boards, I do a quick scan to see if any exist on the board.

FYI: Mis-clicks are easy without a stylus. Zoom is necessary, so don’t be afraid to use it. “Hint” button doesn’t always work. Portrait orientation only. Rotate is backward - see below.

A few improvements: You can’t choose your difficulty level - that would be a nice option after a particularly stressful day. To rotate the forward face, you have to roll it the opposite direction, ie: to rotate clockwise, you have to circle counter-clockwise. author: M1r4G3
title: Needs some work
content:
Basic gameplay is ok -- I like the shapes and 3D gameplay -- but given how many other nearly identical games there are, this needs some improvements. 

Dot grids are a crucial accessibility feature that needs to be an option in the settings — this is NOT an optional nice-to-have. There is no music, no color, and the game frequency misreads taps, counting them as an error. The ads you then have to watch aren't constrained into reasonable timeframes - some are a 90+ second loop of the same ad on repeat. It doesn't save your progress on levels, so you have to start them over, and some "hard"+ ones are complex and very time-consuming, especially with the ads from mis-taps factored in. It's unacceptable to have to start over just because you didn't have time to compete them in one sitting. (I also do not want to be nagged about a hint every 2 seconds. Leave me alone - I’m looking at the board- I do not need to be reminded that hints exist.) 

I don’t need power ups or any of that - I just want a decent, relaxing puzzle game. 

It’s not relaxing or fun to have to restart a hard level, have no music or colors, no grid, one or two maximum “mistakes” (tap misreads!) and then have to watch long, repetitive ads to continue. A few small changes would make this app so great!

author: FondOma
title: New changes are frustrating
content:
In the old version, you had three hearts (or even four or five for the hard levels) and the game kept track of how many arrows you have left. You didn’t get gold, there were no special boosters - clean, simple, challenging, fun. 
Now you get a certain number of moves with no correlation to the number of arrows. Sometimes you only get one false move, even on a hard level (and on these boards, you can’t always see where the arrow will go), so if your finger falls on the wrong line by mistake, you Might be toast, but you won’t know for 40 more moves. 
I love the tricks - two-way arrows, corners that aren’t edges -  but the new way of counting moves? So not a fan
